content.text: {"relation": "MATCH", "consensus_summary": "The consensus identifies the almond (shaqed) primarily as a symbol of God's watchfulness/vigilance over His word, grounded in the Jeremiah 1:11-12 shaqed/shoqed wordplay and the almond's early ('wakeful') blooming. Widely acknowledged secondary strands: divine election and authenticated priesthood via Aaron's budded rod (Num 17:8), sanctuary light via the almond-cup menorah (Ex 25:33-34), old age/white hair (Eccl 12:5), and resurrection/new life as a typological extension.", "book_summary": "The book calls the almond the 'watcher-tree' whose early waking pictures watchfulness, and additionally the sign of the chosen Levitical priesthood via Aaron's fruitful rod, with almond cups carrying the sanctuary lamps—citing Jer 1:11-12, Num 17:8, and Ex 25:33-34.", "consensus_core_identification": "Almond = God's watchfulness/wakefulness over His word (Jeremiah wordplay), with priesthood-election (Aaron's rod) and sanctuary-light (menorah) as recognized companion meanings.", "book_core_identification": "Almond = the watcher-tree (watchfulness from early waking) and sign of the appointed Levitical priesthood, with almond cups bearing the sanctuary lamps.", "core_relation": "EQUIVALENT", "extension_relation": "SAME_CASES", "boundary_disagreement": "None of substance. The book elevates the priesthood strand (Num 17:8) into its headline alongside watchfulness rather than treating it as a subordinate alternative, and it omits the Ecclesiastes 12:5 old-age reading and the standalone resurrection motif; but every element the book asserts appears in the consensus (primary meaning plus its two most common alternatives), and the omissions are not denials.", "material_contradiction": "None. Watchfulness, priestly appointment, and menorah association are all consensus-listed meanings anchored to the same three proof texts the book prints.", "rationale": "The book's core identification—watchfulness via the almond's early waking, joined with Aaron's rod marking the chosen priesthood and the menorah's almond cups—maps directly onto the consensus's primary meaning and its two 'common' alternatives, using identical scriptural anchors (Jer 1:11-12; Num 17:8; Ex 25:33-34). Bundling the priesthood sign into the entry's lead sentence is a matter of emphasis and compression, not a change of referent or boundary. No consensus case is rejected or reclassified, so this is a MATCH rather than REFINED.", "citation_support": "STRONG", "strongest_objection": "One could argue the book makes 'sign of the chosen Levitical priesthood' co-primary rather than secondary, which slightly reweights the consensus hierarchy and could be read as a refinement of emphasis; also, the KJV's Jeremiah 1:12 ('I will hasten my word') obscures the shaqed/shoqed 'watching' wordplay the book's 'watcher-tree' label depends on, so the printed KJV text supports 'hastening' more directly than 'watching.' Neither point alters the shared central identification.", "confidence": "high"}
